newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures expand gains, end higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures expand gains, end higher.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures expanded gains again late and finished pit trading sharply higher as December Standard & Poor's (S&P) 500 futures stretched up to another new all-time high for that contract.
The lead-month S&P 500 futures climbed as high as 739.40 during the final 20 minutes of floor trading and closed up 5.05 points at 739.25.
The afternoon rise drew power from a rebound and strong close in U.S. Treasury bond futures, which ratcheted upward from morning losses to end moderately higher and close to session peaks.
Traders said the last leg of the rise, however, occurred on relatively thin turnover dominated by locals and powered by occasional buystops, which magnified the move higher.
Still, few were willing to step in front of the advance, which they said has kept shorts on edge and quick to cover.
"All week we've been strong. We've been looking for a correction and we're not getting it," said one S&P 500 futures floor broker. "I don't see any reason to change just yet. The movement is up."
Front-month S&P 500s cleared several layers of resistance but stopped short of next levels pegged at 739.60 and 740.45.
Some traders also waited to see whether and how position adjustments ahead of the expiration on Friday afternoon of the November S&P 100 index options affect S&P 500 futures.

On Thursday morning, S&Ps had weakened with T-bond futures and on edginess about published comments by Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin, who reportedly said President Clinton would fight a balanced budget amendment if Republicans proposed one.
Rubin said Clinton sees it as doing little to cut the deficit, while limiting government flexibility.
Futures had muted reaction to consumer price, retail sales and real earnings October data that meshed with forecasts.
